name: Multinomial generalization of the p^{v_p(C(2n,n))} ≤ 2n carry bound

insights: The naive generalization p^{v_p(C(kn;n,...,n))} ≤ kn is FALSE. Smallest counterexample: k=3, n=2, p=3, where the multinomial coefficient is 90 = 2·3²·5, so 3^{v_3}=9 > 6=kn. Verified numerically (132 counterexamples for k∈[2,6], n∈[1,11]) and formalized as naive_multinomial_bound_false.

Mechanism of failure: for the two-term sum n+n each base-p carry is 0/1, so v_p equals the count of carry positions ≤ log_p(2n); for k≥3 copies of n a single column can carry up to k−1, so valuation accumulates faster than one unit per digit position.
The honest bound is p^{v_p} ≤ n^k·k! = ∏_{j=1}^{k}(jn), holding for every prime power (0 numerical violations over k≤7,n≤13,p≤23). A weaker clean form is (kn)^{k-1}.
Product–multinomial identity C(kn;n,...,n)=∏_{j=1}^{k} C(jn,n) is the workhorse: it links the explicit product to the multinomial and computes exact values for the refutation.
